title: docs(releases): curate the 17.4.0 release page — replace the machine draft with release notes in the 17.3.0 shape, and retire the "machine draft" notices on the v17 index
body:
## Maintainer instruction (verbatim, untranslated)

> https://objectstack.ai/docs/releases/v17/17-4 这个文档也要修正

Given in the maintainer's own PM session on 2026-09-10, in the same conversation that ruled for the README rewrites: "数量 相关的统计都去掉", "价值不大的段落都可以删除", "开源项目要想着怎么吸引开发者". Those three sentences were said about `README.md`; they are guidance for tone here, not a second rule.

## What is wrong today

`content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx` is the page the URL above renders. It says so itself, at the top:

> ⚠️ **This page is a machine draft, not curated release notes.** … The content was generated by de-duplicating the **396 changesets** that make up 17.4.0 across all 61 package `CHANGELOG.md` files … and taking each one's own headline verbatim. … No editorial pass: nothing dropped for being internal, nothing merged into a themed narrative, nothing ranked.

Concretely, on `origin/main` at `706ad0f` (read 2026-09-10T08:16Z):

- **Highlights — 17.4.0** reads "⛔ Not written, and deliberately not guessed."
- **Breaking changes & migration in 17.4.0** is a flat list of 35 raw changeset headlines, one bullet each, with a `<span>` of package names under every bullet and no migration prose.
- **New capabilities in 17.4.0** is "Every remaining `minor`-bumping changeset, verbatim." — 140 bullets in package order.
- **Fixes in 17.4.0** is a per-package count table ("`spec` — 50, `cli` — 38, …and 35 further packages").
- **New in Console (Studio)** says "⛔ The intermediate bumps are not enumerated here" and asks "whoever curates this page" to walk the pin history.
- **Upgrade checklist** reads "⛔ **Not written.**"

Two sibling pages carry the same admission and must move in the same PR:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/index.mdx` — the status blockquote ends with a paragraph beginning "⛔ **17.4.0's notes are a machine draft, not curated.**", and the **Upgrade checklists** callout describes which lists have been walked.
- `content/docs/releases/index.mdx` — the v17 entry; check it does not describe 17.4.0 as a draft (on the read above it only says "current series: 17.4.0, released 2026-09-09", which is fine).

## The deliverable

Rewrite `17-4.mdx` into curated release notes with the **same section shape as** `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx` — that page is the model, read it whole first:

1. Frontmatter `description` without the draft marker (e.g. "Release notes and upgrade checklist for 17.4.0 of the v17 line.").
2. `## Highlights — 17.4.0` — a short list of what the release means to a reader, written from the breaking list first (the 17.3.0 page shows the register: one bold lead per item, the commit or issue in parentheses, the migration one-liner where one exists).
3. `## What's new in 17.4.0` → `### Breaking changes & migration in 17.4.0` — group the 35 breaking-marked entries into themed `####` subsections with a **Migration** note each, the way 17.3.0 does (`#### … (#issue)` headings, then a `#### Smaller breaking changes in 17.4.0` list for the rest). ⚠️ The heading text "Breaking changes & migration in 17.4.0" must stay exactly as is — `content/docs/releases/v17/index.mdx` and this page itself link to the anchor `#breaking-changes--migration-in-1740`.
4. `### New capabilities in 17.4.0` — the 140 minor entries grouped by theme and rewritten as prose bullets, not a verbatim dump. Internal-only entries (ledger registrations, `dist` census rows, test-only pins) are dropped or folded into one line.
5. A notable-fixes passage in place of the per-package count table. Source: every `packages/**/CHANGELOG.md` `## 17.4.0` → `### Patch Changes` bullet. Pick the ones a reader upgrading would want to know about (security posture, silent-behaviour changes, wire-shape corrections); leave the rest to the per-package changelogs and say so in one sentence.
6. `### New in Console (Studio) — objectui pins in 17.4.0` — two pin moves carry the console half of this release, both fully recorded in `packages/console/CHANGELOG.md` under `## 17.4.0`: `236f2df` (`00d3f09c500c → a472b07167a3`, 4 declared-breaking entries) and `30b0990` (`a472b07167a3 → 53ded82bf7a4`, 2 declared-breaking entries). Name the breaking entries for console hosts and authors the way 17.3.0's Console section does. Do **not** try to walk objectui's git history: the shallow checkouts here do not carry those SHAs, and the console changelog already lists every declared entry and every no-changeset commit.
7. `## Upgrade checklist` → `### 17.4.0` — derived from the breaking list, in the 17.3.0 checklist's grouping (Getting onto the release / Metadata and build / Data and database / Deployment and configuration / Application code, hooks and flows). ⚠️ Nobody has walked 17.3.0 → 17.4.0. Every line therefore carries the **not exercised** marker, and the section opens by saying so in one sentence, exactly as the v17 index's convention demands ("a step nobody has run, presented beside steps that were, is how a reader finishes a checklist and believes they are done"). Do **not** write "measured". Keep the "Getting onto the release" pin-move step linking `/docs/upgrading#moving-the-dependency-pins`. The heading "Upgrade checklist" must stay — the v17 index links `#upgrade-checklist`.

Then in `content/docs/releases/v17/index.mdx`: delete the "⛔ **17.4.0's notes are a machine draft**" paragraph from the status blockquote (replace it with one sentence that 17.4.0 has its own breaking list and checklist, linking both anchors, in the register of the 17.3.0 sentence just above it), and extend the **Upgrade checklists** callout so it states that the 17.4.0 list is derived, not measured.

## Constraints

- Counts are not the content. At most one sentence of scale (17.3.0's "862 changelog entries, 100 of them self-marked breaking" register is the ceiling); no count tables, no per-package tallies, no "N+" claims anywhere on the page.
- English only. Do not use the reserved word that ADR-0090 D3 forbids in docs (permission set / position / business unit are the spellings) — `node scripts/check-role-word.mjs` is a ratchet and will refuse a new occurrence.
- Quote commit hashes and issue numbers from the changelog entries themselves; do not invent attributions.
- No edits outside `content/docs/releases/`. No changeset: nothing here publishes (the PM applies `skip-changeset` on the PR).
- This is the **dedicated docs-only PR** that `AGENTS.md` names as the route for a releases page ("Factual error on a releases page → dedicated docs-only PR or an issue, never a rider on code changes"). The os-dev rule "never edit `content/docs/releases/`" is the code-PR case of that same table row; AGENTS.md wins. If a hook still blocks the edit, stop and report `blocked` with the hook's text.

## Gates to run before pushing (re-derive for the actual diff; this list is a lead, not the spec)

```
node scripts/check-doc-frontmatter.mjs
node scripts/check-docs-nav-label.mjs
node scripts/check-docs-section-name.mjs
node scripts/check-release-section-coverage.mjs --strict
node scripts/check-section-landing-index.mjs
node scripts/check-doc-route-spelling.mjs --advisory
node scripts/check-role-word.mjs
node scripts/check-doc-anchors.mjs        # needs pnpm install (github-slugger)
pnpm check:release-page-status
pnpm check:release-notes
pnpm check:release-index-currency-sync
```

Also build the docs site once under the shared verify lock (`bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c 'pnpm docs:build'`) so a broken MDX construct is caught here and not in the Build Docs job.

## Acceptance

- The rendered page has no "machine draft", "not written", "not enumerated" or "not guessed" text left, and every section listed above exists with the heading text given.
- `#breaking-changes--migration-in-1740` and `#upgrade-checklist` still resolve.
- The v17 index no longer calls 17.4.0 a draft, and its checklist callout says the 17.4.0 list is derived and not exercised.
- Every gate above green; PR is a draft against `main`, first body line `Fixes #<this issue>`.
